title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that combined social engineering with AI-generated fraud. The attack began with unsolicited contact via WhatsApp, then moved the victim to a real trading app where initial small withdrawals succeeded, building trust. Scammers then deployed a fake AI-generated website displaying false account information to show growing balances while money was being transferred out of the victim's control.

This is a failure of detection at multiple stages. The real trading app itself was legitimate, so it provided no warning signal. The scammers' tool was a fabricated interface that presented false data to the victim, not a misuse of an AI system's actual output. Whether the platform operators could have detected unusual account activity, whether the initial contact vector could have been blocked, or whether the victim had access to independent verification of account status is not established. Investigators reported that recovery is rare in such cases.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were contacted by a stranger who convinced Jerry to invest in cryptocurrency through a mobile trading app. Initially, Jerry made small investments and was able to withdraw modest returns, which built his confidence and trust. Over time, he invested increasingly larger amounts of money into what appeared to be a legitimate trading platform.

The scam unraveled when Jerry attempted a larger withdrawal and found he could not access his funds. Police discovered that while the trading app was real, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false information on Jerry's screen, making him believe his money was growing when it was actually being stolen. The couple is now working with Gwinnett County police, though investigators indicated that victims in these cases rarely recover their funds. The Dunaways are speaking publicly to warn others about the tactics used by scammers, and their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help support them financially.
